transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this workout meeting for the Harbor Point Properties restructuring proposal. As you all know, we have an $8 million term loan secured by the borrower's office building, equipment, and receivables. Harbor Point has requested a 12-month maturity extension, a waiver of the current financial covenant, and release of $900,000 of equipment collateral due to weaker-than-expected occupancy reducing their debt-service coverage. Before I can record the final terms, I need each of you -- risk, relationship coverage, legal, and collateral management -- to provide your findings update and identify the supporting document or policy behind any recommendations. The applicable workout treatment depends on the current covenant test and the supporting policy materials, so we can't finalize this from the borrower's requested terms alone. Let's start with risk. Who's reporting first?

transcript.text: I need to flag what I found in the covenant testing file this week. Leverage is currently 0.3x above the permitted level. Under our workout policy, a covenant waiver is only allowed with a 9-month extension — not the 12 months Harbor Point is requesting — and requires a monthly leverage certificate going forward. I also want to note that I have not yet attached the testing file to the committee package, so I'll make sure that gets added before we finalize anything.

I think this is directly relevant to the covenant situation Jonas just flagged and to the overall restructuring assessment.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical legal issue before we go any further. While reviewing the intercreditor agreement this week, I confirmed that the senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral is released. That consent has not yet been requested. This directly impacts Harbor Point's request to release $900,000 of equipment collateral — we cannot approve that release, or even conditionally agree to it, until the senior lender's written consent is obtained. The intercreditor agreement is the supporting document for this finding.

transcript.text: I completed a collateral review yesterday, and my findings are significant for this restructuring. The review shows that receivables are the weakest and most volatile part of the collateral package. Under our collateral policy, this requires a weekly borrowing-base certificate throughout any extension period. I want to flag that I have not yet updated the monitoring schedule to reflect this requirement, so I'll need to do that before any final terms are recorded. The collateral review and supporting collateral policy are the documents behind this recommendation.
